name: dup
text: Copy the top item.
examples: : sq dup * ;
: fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;
epin @ pin@ dup elast @ <> if 1 ecount +! then elast !

name: drop
text: Remove the top item.
examples: 10 low $9F 0 spi-xfer drop 0 0 spi-xfer . 10 high
$48 0 i2c-addr drop 0 i2c-write drop
$48 1 i2c-addr drop -1 i2c-read 8 lshift 0 i2c-read or i2c-stop ;

name: swap
text: Exchange the top two items.
examples: accel@ rot . swap . . 0 0 1000  ok   \ x y z, the board lying flat
wait-btn ms@ swap - 0 led!
: level ( -- n ) 3 adc@ 9 4096 */ 1 swap lshift 1- ;

name: over
text: Copy the second item to the top.
examples: ms@ over - 499 > if 5 toggle show drop ms@ then

name: nip
text: Remove the second item.
examples: : up? accel@ nip nip 0> if ." face up" else ." face down" then cr ;

name: tuck
text: Copy the top item below the second.
examples: : span ( -- min max ) 32767 -32768 64 0 do i sample @ tuck max >r min r> loop ;

name: rot
stack: ( a b c -- b c a )
text: Rotate the third item to the top.
examples: accel@ rot . swap . . 0 0 1000  ok   \ x y z, the board lying flat
: tilt begin accel@ rot . swap . . cr 500 ms key? until key drop ;

name: -rot
stack: ( a b c -- c a b )
text: Rotate the top item to third place.

name: 2dup
stack: ( a b -- a b a b )
text: Copy the top two items.

name: 2drop
text: Remove the top two items.
examples: : x-led ( -- n ) accel@ 2drop 1000 + 250 / 0 max 7 min ;

name: ?dup
text: Copy the top item only if it is not zero.

name: depth
text: Number of items on the data stack, before depth itself pushes.

name: .s
text: Show the stack without changing it: <3> 1 2 3, with the depth and the top on the right.

name: >r
text: Move the top item to the return stack.
examples: : span ( -- min max ) 32767 -32768 64 0 do i sample @ tuck max >r min r> loop ;

name: r>
text: Move the top of the return stack back.
examples: : span ( -- min max ) 32767 -32768 64 0 do i sample @ tuck max >r min r> loop ;

name: r@
text: Copy the top of the return stack.
Sum.

: five [ 2 3 + ] literal ;  ok
: x-led ( -- n ) accel@ 2drop 1000 + 250 / 0 max 7 min ;

examples: : level ( -- n ) 3 adc@ 9 4096 */ 1 swap lshift 1- ;

pot dup bar 1000 3300 */ 0 pwm-duty

text: Full 32-bit unsigned product as two cells, the high cell on top: -1 -1 um* gives 1 −2 (65534).

Add one.

examples: : x-led ( -- n ) accel@ 2drop 1000 + 250 / 0 max 7 min ;

name: max
text: Larger of two signed numbers.
examples: : x-led ( -- n ) accel@ 2drop 1000 + 250 / 0 max 7 min ;
: span ( -- min max ) 32767 -32768 64 0 do i sample @ tuck max >r min r> loop ;

name: umin
text: Smaller of two unsigned numbers: -1 3 umin gives 3.

name: and
text: Bitwise AND.
examples: $81 led!   \ LED1 and LED8 on, all others off
3 led-on   \ LED3 on as well: LED1, LED3 and LED8 are lit
1 led-off   \ LED1 off: LED3 and LED8 stay on

name: or
text: Bitwise OR.
examples: $48 1 i2c-addr drop -1 i2c-read 8 lshift 0 i2c-read or i2c-stop ;
: f@ ( lo hi -- x ) f-read 0 spi 0 spi f-end 8 lshift or ;  ok
: f@ ( lo hi -- x ) f-read 0 spi 0 spi f-end 8 lshift or ;

name: xor
text: Bitwise exclusive OR.

name: invert
text: Invert all bits. Also turns a true flag into false and back.

name: lshift
text: Shift left by u bits; u ≥ 16 gives 0.
examples: $48 1 i2c-addr drop -1 i2c-read 8 lshift 0 i2c-read or i2c-stop ;
: f@ ( lo hi -- x ) f-read 0 spi 0 spi f-end 8 lshift or ;  ok
: runner begin 8 0 do 1 i lshift led! 100 ms loop key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: rshift
text: Logical shift right by u bits (fills with 0); u ≥ 16 gives 0.
Equal.
examples: 10 output 10 high   \ D10 = chip select, idle high
: find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;
key? if key dup 27 = if drop exit then 0 uart-emit then

1000 0 pwm-hz  0 pwm @ u. 48000  ok

examples: variable x  5 x !  3 x +!  x ? 8  ok
255 $8014 !   \ D0..D7 as outputs
170 $8012 !   \ D1, D3, D5, D7 high, the others low

name: c@
text: Fetch the byte at a.

name: c!
text: Store the low byte of c at a.
Add n to the cell at addr.
examples: variable x  5 x !  3 x +!  x ? 8  ok
: bump 1 count +! ;

text: Print the cell at a, like @ ..
examples: variable x  5 x !  3 x +!  x ? 8  ok
table 2 cells + ? 4  ok

examples: table 2 cells + ? 4  ok
: sample ( i -- a ) cells samples + ;

name: cell+
text: Address of the next cell.

name: aligned
text: Round a up to an even address.

name: cmove
text: Copy n bytes from src to dst, lowest address first.

name: here
text: Address of the next free byte.

name: allot
text: Reserve n bytes at here (a negative n gives memory back).
examples: create buffer 20 allot

name: align
text: Make here even.
Align, store x at here, advance by one cell.
examples: create table 1 , 2 , 4 , 8 ,

name: c,
text: Store a byte at here, advance by one byte.

name: unused
text: Free code space: $4000"minus "here.

text: Reserve n bytes of data RAM (rounded up to even, so cells stay aligned); name"then pushes their address. " data RAM full if fewer than n bytes are left.
examples: 100 buffer: buf  ok
128 buffer: samples

name: unused-data
text: Free data RAM in bytes.
examples: buf . unused-data . 16384 7068  ok

name: key
text: Wait for a character from the terminal. Answers the app's requests while it waits.
examples: : runner begin 8 0 do 1 i lshift led! 100 ms loop key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: alternate ( -- )   \ LED1 and LED2 take turns; any key stops
begin 1 led-toggle 2 led-toggle 250 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: key?
text: True if a character is waiting (does not take it). Answers the app's requests waiting before it.
examples: : runner begin 8 0 do 1 i lshift led! 100 ms loop key? until key drop 0 led! ;
begin 1 led-toggle 2 led-toggle 250 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: emit
text: Send a character (waits while the 1 KB send FIFO is full).
examples: : show ( -- ) begin 0 uart-key? while 0 uart-key emit repeat ;
0 uart-key? if 0 uart-key emit then

name: cr
text: New line (sends CR and LF).
examples: : hello ." Hello, MAX1000!" cr ;
." wait for the LEDs..." cr
." reaction time " . ." ms" cr

name: space
text: Send one space.

name: spaces
text: Send n spaces (nothing for n ≤ 0).

name: type
text: Send n characters starting at a.
Print a signed number in the current base, then a space.
examples: buf . unused-data . 16384 7068  ok
led@ .   \ prints 132 ($84)
btn@ .   \ hold the USER button while pressing Enter: prints -1

name: u.
text: Print an unsigned number, then a space: -1 u. gives 65535.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  0 pwm @ u. 48000  ok
hex crc-test u. u. decimal CBF4 3926  ok

text: Compile only: print text when the definition runs.
examples: : hello ." Hello, MAX1000!" cr ;
: find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;
: shout ." loud" ; immediate

text: Print text immediately, in a definition or at the terminal.

name: base
text: Variable holding the base for number input and output (2..36).

name: hex
text: Set the base to 16.
examples: 1000 dds-hz  $8060 @ hex . decimal 5762  ok
hex flash-id . . . decimal 17 40 EF  ok
hex crc-test u. u. decimal CBF4 3926  ok

name: decimal
text: Set the base to 10.
examples: 1000 dds-hz  $8060 @ hex . decimal 5762  ok
hex flash-id . . . decimal 17 40 EF  ok
hex crc-test u. u. decimal CBF4 3926  ok

name: led!
text: Set LED1..LED8 from bits 0..7 of n (1 = on; bit 0 = LED1).
examples: $81 led!   \ LED1 and LED8 on, all others off
: count256 256 0 do i led! 30 ms loop 0 led! ;
: runner begin 8 0 do 1 i lshift led! 100 ms loop key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: led@
text: Read back the LED state.
examples: led@ .   \ prints 132 ($84)

name: led-on
text: Switch LED n (1..8) on; the other LEDs stay as they are.
examples: 3 led-on   \ LED3 on as well: LED1, LED3 and LED8 are lit
0 led! 1 led-on

name: led-off
text: Switch LED n (1..8) off; the other LEDs stay as they are.
examples: 1 led-off   \ LED1 off: LED3 and LED8 stay on

name: led-toggle
text: Change LED n (1..8): on becomes off, off becomes on.
examples: : blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;
begin 1 led-toggle 2 led-toggle 250 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: led-mask
text: The bit of LED n in led!"(1 for LED1 … 128 for LED8); " bad led for n outside 1..8.

name: btn@
text: The USER button: true while pressed. Debounced (sampled every 10 ms).
examples: btn@ .   \ hold the USER button while pressing Enter: prints -1
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: wait-btn begin btn@ until ;

name: ms
text: Wait n milliseconds (0..32767). Answers the app's requests while it waits.
examples: : blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  4 1 pwm-pin   \ D4: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses
: count256 256 0 do i led! 30 ms loop 0 led! ;

name: ms@
text: Millisecond counter; wraps every 65.536 s.
examples: 2000 ms 255 led! ms@
wait-btn ms@ swap - 0 led!
ms@ + begin

name: output
text: Make pin n an output.
examples: 3 output  3 high   \ D3 to 3.3 V
10 output 10 high   \ D10 = chip select, idle high
: blink3 3 output begin 3 toggle 250 ms key? until key drop 3 low ;

name: input
text: Make pin n an input again.
examples: 3 low  3 input   \ back to an input
0 output  0 high  1 pin@ .  0 low  1 pin@ .  0 input
3 output  3 high  10 ms  0 mv@ .  3 low  10 ms  0 mv@ .  3 input

name: high
text: Set the pin's output latch to 1 (3.3 V when it is an output).
examples: 3 output  3 high   \ D3 to 3.3 V
1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  3 0 pwm-pin   \ D3: 1 kHz, 25 % high
10 output 10 high   \ D10 = chip select, idle high

name: low
text: Set the output latch to 0.
examples: 3 low  3 input   \ back to an input
170 $8012 !   \ D1, D3, D5, D7 high, the others low
10 low $9F 0 spi-xfer drop 0 0 spi-xfer . 10 high

name: toggle
text: Invert the output latch.
examples: : blink3 3 output begin 3 toggle 250 ms key? until key drop 3 low ;
ms@ over - 499 > if 5 toggle show drop ms@ then

name: pin!
text: high"if f is true, otherwise "low.
examples: 6 pin@ 0= 4 pin!

name: pin@
text: Read the level at the pin: true = high. Also works on outputs, where it reads back the driven level.
examples: 3 pin@ . -1  ok
: watch6 begin 6 pin@ 0= 1 and led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
0 output  0 high  1 pin@ .  0 low  1 pin@ .  0 input

name: pin
text: Bit mask and port address of pin n; "bad pin" for numbers that are not pins.
examples: : edges ( pin ms -- n )   \ level changes on the pin within ms milliseconds

name: bset
text: Set the mask bits in the cell at a (a general helper).

name: bclr
text: Clear the mask bits in the cell at a.

name: owner
text: Who has pin n (section 5.15): 0 = nobody (the pin follows its latch and direction), 1..4 = PWM channel 0..3, 5, 6 = UART 0, 1, 7, 8 = SPI 0, 1, 9 = I2C, 10 = DDS.

name: adc@
text: Raw result of input n (0..8, the table above): 0..4095 for 0 to 3.3 V. "bad input" for other numbers.
examples: : level ( -- n ) 3 adc@ 9 4096 */ 1 swap lshift 1- ;

name: mv@
text: The input's voltage in millivolts: 0..3299.
examples: 3 mv@ . 1650  ok   \ for example: a potentiometer half way
: volts begin 3 mv@ . ." mV" cr 500 ms key? until key drop ;
3 output  3 high  10 ms  0 mv@ .  3 low  10 ms  0 mv@ .  3 input

name: adc-ch@
text: Raw result of ADC channel c, 0..8, in the converter's own numbering; 9 is the temperature diode.

name: ain
text: Table of 9 bytes: the ADC channel of each input (used by adc@).

name: temp-code@
text: Raw code of the temperature sensing diode, a running average of 64 samples. It falls as the chip warms.
examples: temp-code@ . 3640  ok

name: temp@
text: Chip temperature in tenths of a degree Celsius: 346 means 34.6 °C.

name: .temp
text: Print the chip temperature, for example 34.6 C.
examples: .temp 34.6 C  ok
: thermo begin .temp cr 1000 ms key? until key drop ;

name: pwm-pin
text: Route channel ch to the pin and start it. The pin becomes an output driven by the channel; "bad pin" for numbers that are not pins, "pin taken" if another channel, the DDS or a serial interface has it. A channel that had another pin lets it go.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  3 0 pwm-pin   \ D3: 1 kHz, 25 % high
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  4 1 pwm-pin   \ D4: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses
1000 0 pwm-hz  100 0 pwm-duty  3 0 pwm-pin   \ 10 % brightness

name: pwm-off
text: Stop the channel. Its pin returns to its own latch and direction (an input after start-up).
examples: 0 pwm-off  1 pwm-off
0 pwm-off
begin ramp-up ramp-down key? until key drop 0 pwm-off ;

name: pwm-hz
text: Frequency in Hz, 1..65535; "bad frequency" for 0.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  3 0 pwm-pin   \ D3: 1 kHz, 25 % high
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  4 1 pwm-pin   \ D4: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses
1000 0 pwm-hz  0 pwm @ u. 48000  ok

name: pwm-khz
text: Frequency in kHz, 1..24000; "bad frequency" outside.
examples: 10 0 pwm-khz  3 0 pwm-pin

name: pwm-duty
text: Duty cycle in ‰ (tenths of a percent), 0..1000: 0 is always low, 1000 always high; values outside are clamped.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  3 0 pwm-pin   \ D3: 1 kHz, 25 % high
500 0 pwm-duty   \ now 50 %
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  4 1 pwm-pin   \ D4: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses

name: pwm-clocks
text: The period directly, in 48 MHz clocks (20.8 ns), as a double number: low cell, then high cell. At least 2.

name: pwm
text: Register address of channel ch; "bad channel" for ch above 3.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  0 pwm @ u. 48000  ok

name: ud/u
text: Unsigned double divided by an unsigned single, giving a double quotient (used by pwm-hz).

name: dds-hz
text: Frequency in Hz, 0..65535.
examples: 1000 dds-hz  3 dds-pin   \ D3: 1 kHz
1000 dds-hz  $8060 @ hex . decimal 5762  ok
1000 dds-hz  3 dds-pin  3 1000 edges .  dds-off

name: dds-khz
text: Frequency in kHz, 0..65535 (up to 65.5 MHz).
examples: 1500 dds-khz   \ now 1.5 MHz

name: dds-tuning
text: The phase step directly: f = ud × 192 MHz / 2³² (low cell, then high cell).

name: dds-pin
text: Route the DDS to the pin and start it at phase 0; "bad pin" for numbers that are not pins, "pin taken" if a PWM channel or a serial interface has it.
examples: 1000 dds-hz  3 dds-pin   \ D3: 1 kHz
1000 dds-hz  3 dds-pin  3 1000 edges .  dds-off
100 dds-hz 7 dds-pin

name: dds-off
text: Stop it; the pin returns to its own latch and direction.
examples: dds-off
1000 dds-hz  3 dds-pin  3 1000 edges .  dds-off
100 0 do i 100 * 100 + dds-hz 20 ms loop dds-off ;

name: dds-sync

examples: 0 uart-close

name: uart-emit

key? if key dup 27 = if drop exit then 0 uart-emit then

name: uart-type

name: uart-key?

name: uart-key

examples: : show ( -- ) begin 0 uart-key? while 0 uart-key emit repeat ;
0 uart-key? if 0 uart-key emit then

name: uart-status

name: spi-open

name: spi-khz

name: spi-mode

name: spi-lsb

name: spi-bits
text: 8 or 16 bits per transfer; "bad bits" for anything else.

name: spi-xfer
text: Send out and return what came back at the same time (8 or 16 bits).

name: spi-write

name: spi-read
text: Receive n bytes into a, sending zeros.

name: i2c-open
text: Open with SCL and SDA on the given pins; 100 = standard, 400 = fast mode; the clock is at most the value given. "bad frequency" outside 1..1000.
examples: 100 18 19 i2c-open

name: i2c-close
text: Close it; the pins are free again.
examples: i2c-close

text: Write byte b into register reg of the device at addr.
examples: 65 0 $50 i2c!  5 ms   \ 65 into cell 0; writing takes 5 ms

name: i2c@
text: Read register reg of the device at addr (a write of reg, a repeated start, a read).

name: i2c-probe
text: True if a device acknowledges addr.

name: i2c-scan
text: Print the addresses $08..$77 that answer, in hex.
examples: i2c-scan   \ prints 50

name: i2c-start
text: A start condition (or a repeated start).

name: i2c-stop
text: A stop condition.
examples: $48 1 i2c-addr drop -1 i2c-read 8 lshift 0 i2c-read or i2c-stop ;

text: A start, then the address byte: rw 0 = write, 1 = read. True if the device acknowledged.
examples: $48 0 i2c-addr drop 0 i2c-write drop
$48 1 i2c-addr drop -1 i2c-read 8 lshift 0 i2c-read or i2c-stop ;

text: Send a byte; true if the device acknowledged.
examples: $48 0 i2c-addr drop 0 i2c-write drop

name: i2c-read
text: Receive a byte; true: acknowledge it (more will be read), false: it is the last.
examples: $48 1 i2c-addr drop -1 i2c-read 8 lshift 0 i2c-read or i2c-stop ;

name: accel@
text: The acceleration on the three axes in mg (thousandths of g). Lying flat, components up, the board reads about 0 0 1000.

text: True if the accelerometer answers (its WHO_AM_I register reads $33).

name: accel-on

name: acc@

name: acc!

examples: : f@ ( lo hi -- x ) f-read 0 spi 0 spi f-end 8 lshift or ;  ok
